claims.text: Adding 2 at.% boron to refractory high-entropy alloys will improve ductility by 30% relative to an untreated baseline.
Adding 2 at.% boron to refractory high-entropy alloys will improve uniform deformability by 30% relative to an untreated baseline.
The 2 at.% boron addition will not sacrifice high strength.
The 2 at.% boron addition will not sacrifice impact-induced energy release.
Adding 2 at.% boron will refine the alloy grain size.
Adding 2 at.% boron will modify the alloy phase composition.
Boron-induced grain refinement will produce grain-boundary strengthening.
The boron-induced modification of phase composition will produce phase-transformation toughening.
Grain-boundary strengthening and phase-transformation toughening will improve ductility and uniform deformability while retaining strength.
The proposed benefits will hold under high-stress, high-strain-rate operating conditions.
The magnitude of improvement may depend on the specific refractory high-entropy-alloy composition and processing conditions.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis predicts a 30% improvement, but the falsification rule accepts improvements between 20% and 30% as non-falsifying, so it does not decisively test the stated quantitative prediction.
The hypothesis states that strength and impact-induced energy release will not be sacrificed, whereas the falsification rule permits losses of up to 10%.
